messages.subject: Help sampling design
parts:
Dear,

I am starting a project and looking for some advice on the sampling design before conducting fieldwork in order to have a precise estimate.

I am working with a bird specie which has superpopulation in cities, spreads over the whole city, has big home range but they are mainly found concentrated in communal roosts and feeding sites.

So I was wondering I could have our
option about how could I use distance sampling design and wheter this would be a good method to archive what I want ornot. I need to estimate the total population size in the city.

I am considering doing count points across the city. However I suppose that because of the fact of birds are aggregated it is thereby violating one of the assuptions of DS.

How could I do it?

Thank you so much in advance,
Suggestions are very appreciated.
Best regards,
Rafael

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Help sampling design
parts:
Rafael

Aggregation of animals does not violate any distance sampling
assumptions; no distribution of animals across the study area is assumed
by distance sampling.  The design assumption of distance sampling
(Buckland et al 2015 Section 1.7) is that animals are distributed
uniformly at all distances from the line *out to the truncation
distance* for lines and distributed according to a triangular
distribution for points.

However line transect distance sampling was intended for use with
populations that are sparsely distributed.  With the concentration at
roost sites, an observer will struggle to record distances to many many
individuals.  It might be the case that a hybrid stratified approach,
using perhaps photos to count animals in high density strata such as
roost sites and possibly point transects in a medium density stratum in
city parklands.  There might be a low-density stratum in built-up areas
of the city where birds are unlikely to be located. However, care will
need to be take to ensure the triangular distribution of birds at points.
